rack_air_gpu.name: Mk.I Air-Cooled Compute Cabinet
rack_air_gpu.description: Four 8-GPU servers in a putty-enamel mainframe cabinet, breathing aisle air through a punch-card intake. Around 40 kW per cabinet is where air cooling gives up. Ministry Form CC-1 applies.

rack_dlc_gpu.name: Mk.II Liquid-Plumbed Compute Cabinet
rack_dlc_gpu.description: A 72-GPU NVLink cabinet with copper cold plates bolted to every die, drawing about 120 kW. Roughly 80% of its heat leaves through the brass manifold, so it must be plumbed into a coolant loop.

rack_storage.name: Magnetic Archive Cabinet
rack_storage.description: Spinning tape reels and drive shelves holding the datasets and checkpoints that training jobs stream from. Every byte is filed in triplicate.

crah_unit.name: Air Handler (Fans Zip-Tied)
crah_unit.description: A computer-room air handler with its own compressor and three desk fans zip-tied on for good measure. Pulls hot air from aisles within about 8 tiles and returns it chilled.

chiller.name: Steam-Vented Chiller
chiller.description: A riveted boiler-tank chiller that rejects coolant-loop heat outdoors, spending about 1 kW of electricity per 5.5 kW of heat moved. Works less well on hot days.

cdu.name: Coolant Distribution Manifold
cdu.description: A heat exchanger, pump and wall of brass valve wheels that feeds warm-water cold plates from the facility loop. Liquid cabinets on its loop are capped by its capacity.

grid_tie.name: Municipal Grid Intake
grid_tie.description: Porcelain insulators, a knife switch and a step-down transformer on the city's high-voltage main. Imports up to 1.5 MW at the going rate.

genset.name: Diesel Generator No. 4
genset.description: An 800 kW green-enamel diesel that cranks itself when the net runs short. It takes about 10 minutes to come up to speed, and the fuel bill is not small.

ups_battery.name: Accumulator Bank
ups_battery.description: Rows of glass-jar cells behind a double-conversion rectifier: 250 kWh that bridges outages until the generator wakes up. Watch the charge needle.

parts_depot.name: Spare Parts Requisition Cage
parts_depot.description: A wire cage of stamped crates holding spare GPU trays, PSUs and pumps. Failures are routine at scale, so keep it stocked. Requisitions on Form 27B/6.

bot_charger.name: Automaton Docking Station
bot_charger.description: Brass docking bays where maintenance automatons recharge at 5 kW through a pantograph arm. New units are delivered here.

rack_air_gpu2.name: Mk.III Rear-Door Air Cabinet
rack_air_gpu2.description: Eight-GPU trays behind a hinged water-cooled rear door that scrubs the exhaust before it reaches the aisle. 55 kW and 32 PFLOPS per cabinet, but it needs an air handler that can keep up.

rack_air_gpu3.name: Mk.IV Hot-Aisle Air Cabinet
rack_air_gpu3.description: A sealed hot-aisle cabinet with ducted exhaust and tuned fan curves, squeezing 52 PFLOPS out of 70 kW of air-cooled silicon. The practical ceiling of air; the Ministry stamps it 'Adequate'.

rack_dlc_gpu2.name: Mk.III Cold-Plate Compute Cabinet
rack_dlc_gpu2.description: A 160 kW cabinet with cold plates on every die and 82% of its heat carried off by the brass manifold: 230 PFLOPS per cabinet. Needs a coolant loop with a CDU and chiller sized for 131 kW per rack.

rack_dlc_gpu3.name: Mk.IV Manifold Blade Cabinet
rack_dlc_gpu3.description: Rack-scale blades on blind-mate manifolds, 85% liquid-cooled: 240 kW and 420 PFLOPS per cabinet, the best ratio the Ministry has ever signed off. Needs a 204 kW share of coolant capacity.

rack_imm_gpu.name: Mk.I Dielectric Bath Cabinet
rack_imm_gpu.description: Servers submerged in a tank of mineral-oil dielectric, 95% of the 180 kW leaving through the heat exchanger: 300 PFLOPS per tank and a calm 0.15 failures a day. Messy to service, silent to run.

rack_imm_gpu2.name: Mk.II Two-Phase Immersion Vat
rack_imm_gpu2.description: A boiling-fluid vat in a riveted steel tank. 300 kW and 560 PFLOPS per vat, 95% of the heat taken by the condenser coil. The vat bubbles; the Ministry insists this is intended.

rack_infer.name: Inference Accelerator Cabinet
rack_infer.description: Fixed-function inference cards on punched-card firmware: 54 PFLOPS from only 36 kW, so 1.5 PFLOPS per kW, three times the Mk.I. Air-cooled and thrifty with the electricity bill, though it costs $1.3M.

rack_storage2.name: Tape Silo Array
rack_storage2.description: A robotic tape library: 8,000 TB behind glass, retrieved by a gantry arm with opinions. Draws 30 kW and gives training jobs four times the storage of the Archive Cabinet.

grid_tie_2.name: Substation Intake Hall
grid_tie_2.description: A tiled hall of oil-filled transformers on a dedicated 11 kV feeder. Imports up to 3.5 MW at the going rate, with a canteen for the linesmen.

grid_tie_3.name: Transmission Feeder Annex
grid_tie_3.description: A private 132 kV feeder with its own switchyard and a lightning-rod collection. Imports up to 9 MW; the Ministry has asked that you not tell the neighbours.

genset_gas.name: Gas Turbine Set No. 2
genset_gas.description: A 3 MW turbine on a pipeline tap, spun up in about 6 minutes and burning fuel at $18 per kWh (the diesel No. 4 costs $25). Rated for outages, not for vanity.

ups_flywheel.name: Flywheel Rotor Bank
ups_flywheel.description: A hall of vacuum-sealed brass rotors spinning at ten thousand revolutions. Dumps 2 MW instantly but stores only 60 kWh, so it bridges the 10 minutes until a generator wakes up. 97% efficient.

ups_bank_big.name: Accumulator Hall
ups_bank_big.description: Row upon row of lead-acid jars in a ventilated hall: 2,400 kWh at up to 2 MW, 92% round-trip efficient. Rides through long outages and the evening price peak.

crah_rear_door.name: Rear-Door Air Handler
crah_rear_door.description: A slim air handler on a chilled-water coil, mounted at the end of the row: 320 kW of heat removal within 5 tiles. Short reach, strong lungs.

crah_hc.name: High-Capacity Air Handler
crah_hc.description: A roof-sized air handler with a five-blade fan wall: 700 kW of heat removal within 12 tiles. It hums in the key of B-flat.

chiller_tower.name: Cooling-Tower Chiller
chiller_tower.description: A cooling tower on top of a steel chiller set: 2,400 kW of coolant heat rejected at COP 7.0 (1 kW of electricity per 7 kW of heat). The plume is visible from the Ministry.

cdu_big.name: Industrial Coolant Manifold
cdu_big.description: A wall of valve wheels and plate exchangers sized for a whole row: 1,600 kW of liquid-cabinet heat on its loop.

chiller_free.name: Adiabatic Free-Cooling Chiller
chiller_free.description: Louvred halls that spray and evaporate to chill the loop without much compressor: 5,000 kW at COP 11. Steam rises. The Ministry takes credit.

depot_big.name: Central Stores Warehouse
depot_big.description: A hangar of numbered pigeonholes holding 60 spare parts, enough for a bad week. Requisitions on Form 27B/6, countersigned.

charger_fast.name: Pantograph Fast-Charge Bay
charger_fast.description: A four-bay dock with a 25 kW pantograph per berth and a bell that rings when an automaton is full. Bots return to work sooner.

nutrient_plant.name: Nutrient Medium Works
nutrient_plant.description: Copper vats of warm, faintly sweet broth, stirred by a clockwork paddle and piped out through sweating brass. Supplies 20 units of nutrient medium a tick to its pipe net, at $2 a unit. Organoid cabinets and bio-reactors drink from it; do not ask what it is made of.

sterile_bay.name: Sterile Bay
sterile_bay.description: A tiled alcove of ultraviolet lamps, bleach spigots and a drain with a very good reputation. Scrubs contamination from every cell within 6 tiles on its floor (0.0012 a tick at full power). One bay keeps a small annex of two incubators clean.

culling_room.name: Culling Room
culling_room.description: A white-tiled chamber with a hose, a hatch and a rota. Scrubs contamination twice as hard as a Sterile Bay (0.0025 a tick within 7 tiles) and is the only thing the Ministry permits to remove an unregistered growth. Please do not linger.

quarantine_lock.name: Quarantine Lock
quarantine_lock.description: A one-tile airlock of rubber gaskets and a hissing door, stamped with a yellow chevron. Contamination crosses it at only 5% of the normal rate, which is why it is also the most popular place to stand during a fire drill.

bioreactor.name: Bio-Reactor
bioreactor.description: A glass-fronted tank of fermenting broth driving a turbine through a belt. Burns 14 units of nutrient medium a tick for up to 500 kW, about $3.4 a kWh at the medium's price, and leaks 0.0025 contamination a tick into each tile it stands on. Cheap power with a smell.

organoid_incubator.name: Organoid Incubator Cabinet
organoid_incubator.description: A jar-lined cabinet of cultured tissue on a warm nutrient drip, computing 135 PFLOPS from only 24 kW: 5.6 PFLOPS per kW, three times the best air or liquid cabinet. It must be held at 37 °C within 1 °C, and fed 3 units of nutrient medium a tick. It sheds contamination while it works.

dna_vault.name: DNA Vault
dna_vault.description: Helical archives of synthesised strands in a chilled glass cabinet: 16,000 TB from 8 kW, twice the Tape Silo Array. Kept at 28 °C within 4 °C on a thin nutrient drip. The Ministry files it under 'Libraries (Living)'.

neural_pit.name: Neural Pit
neural_pit.description: A four-tile sunken vat of lattice and warm broth, stepped like an amphitheatre for the benefit of no one. 460 PFLOPS from 80 kW: 5.75 PFLOPS per kW. Must be held at 37 °C within 1 °C, drinks 10 units of nutrient medium a tick, and is the most contaminating thing the Ministry has ever licensed.

growth_mass.name: Unregistered Organoid Mass
growth_mass.description: A damp, warm, load-bearing lump of tissue that was not on the plans. It computes 24 PFLOPS on nothing at all, fails often and mends itself. Listed by the Ministry as an asset.

growth_cyst.name: Archival Cyst
growth_cyst.description: A pale sac in the corner of an empty room, holding 300 TB of something that is certainly data. Free storage with a mind of its own. Listed by the Ministry as an asset.

growth_lobe.name: Registered Lobe
growth_lobe.description: A ribbed, glistening bulk that has begun to hum along with the muzak. It computes 60 PFLOPS for free, fails more than most and sheds contamination twice as fast as a mass. Listed by the Ministry as a capital asset.
